C-DROPBOX-CONTENT-REQUEST-FIX.Summary: Correct Dropbox content requests and permission diagnostics within the previously approved save/load work.
C-DROPBOX-CONTENT-REQUEST-FIX.Problem: After successful Chrome authorization, save/load report HTTP 400. Downloads incorrectly include the upload Content-Type header, and plain-text HTTP 400 scope failures lose their actionable explanation.

Goals.Goal: Send Dropbox download requests without a Content-Type header or body while retaining binary upload requests.
Recognize documented permission failures and distinguish unresolved request failures without exposing provider response bodies.

Constraints.Constraint: Preserve encrypted credentials, PKCE, token refresh, transfer bounds, atomic restore, and existing keyboard behavior.
Do not access the real user database or Dropbox account during automated verification.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Change Safari configuration, OAuth flow, remote backup format, or local persistence.
Claim that the upload failure is diagnosed from its status alone.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Downloads omit Content-Type and send an empty body; uploads retain application/octet-stream and snapshot bytes.
HTTP 400 documented scope failures show the required file permission and relinking instructions; unknown responses remain sanitized and include HTTP status.
A real local HTTP server rejects the old download request and verifies a successful save/load round trip with corrected requests.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Deterministic HTTP wire-contract and sanitized permission-error regressions, without live credentials.

Assumptions.Assumption: The user's explicit approval and execution instruction for C-DROPBOX-SAVE-LOAD covers correcting demonstrated application defects in those same requests. This is sequential corrective work, with no additional product scope.
The user confirms consent succeeds in Chrome; Safari failure remains browser-specific and outside this correction.
